chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibrahim ibn Abi Sammaak from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Do not eat anything from the game, even if a person in the state of ihram hunted it. There is no compensation (fidyah) upon you for anything you ate while you were in the state of ihram, being ignorant of it, if you were in ihram for your Hajj or 'Umrah, except for the game; for upon you is the compensation whether it was by ignorance or by choice, because Allah has made it obligatory upon you. If you caught it while you were in the state of ihram in the sanctuary (Haram), then upon you is one compensation. If you caught it while you were in the state of ihram in the non-sanctuary (Hill), then upon you is the compensation. If you caught it while you were in the state of ihram in the sanctuary, then upon you is double the compensation.

And whichever group of people gathered for hunting and ate from it, then upon every person among them is a compensation, one for each. And if they gathered upon it in hunting, then upon them is the same.

key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca/Medina where specific rules apply)
key_terms.فِدَاء: Compensation or ransom (usually in the form of food or animals)
key_terms.قِيمَة: Value/compensation (the equivalent value of the game)
key_terms.مُحْرِم: One in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or 'Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for eating game while in ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the prohibition of hunting applies strictly to the state of ihram, distinguishing it from general consumption. The text establishes a nuanced legal hierarchy where compensation (fidyah) is mandatory regardless of intent, with penalties escalating based on the sanctity of the location (Haram vs. Hill) and the collective liability of the hunting party.
